subject: Prepay proration & rollback clauses — Engage.ai
messages:
From: Lisa Monroe <lisa@engage.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Prepay proration & rollback clauses for Engage.ai

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to confirm how Redwood handles multi-year prepay proration and refund mechanics if we need to reduce seats or terminate early. Specific questions:
- For an annual prepay that rolls into a 3-year commitment, do you pro-rate refunds month-by-month or apply a fixed early-exit penalty?
- If Engage.ai ramps slower than committed in year 1, can unused prepaid dollars roll forward, or are they forfeited?
- What does Redwood expect in terms of contract co-terming if we have existing cloud spend to align?

We'd like a couple of concrete scenarios (e.g., 12-month prepay converted to 36-month, mid-term 40% reduction in seats) and the dollar math so procurement can sign off. Can you send a short matrix and any preferred contract language? We may need your legal team to review any rollback wording.

Thanks,
Lisa Monroe
Director, Procurement
Engage.ai
[Attachment: Engage_SOW_v2.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Monroe <lisa@engage.ai>, procurement@engage.ai
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-30T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Prepay proration & rollback clauses for Engage.ai

Hi Lisa — thanks for the clear list. Attached is a first-pass proration matrix (Prepay_Prorate_Matrix_v1.xlsx) and a redline of the rollback language we usually propose (Redwood_Rollback_Clause_redline.docx). High-level summary below: 

Options we recommend (illustrative):
1) Monthly pro-rata refund: unused prepaid funds are returned on a month-by-month basis for the unconsumed term, less a 5% administrative fee. Best when customer prefers cash recovery.
2) Credit roll-forward with decay: unused prepay rolls forward as credits for up to 12 months, decaying at 25% annually after year one. This preserves customer upside while protecting unit economics.
3) Early-exit fee model: for multi-year prepay converted from annual, apply an early-exit charge equal to 50% of the remaining prepay balance. This is simpler to administer and common on committed discounts.

Co-terming note: we can align renewal dates via a true-up clause. If Engage.ai has existing cloud contracts to co-term, we typically allow pro-rated alignment at next renewal with a one-time adjustment invoice (no retrospective cash refunds).

I included three numeric scenarios in the matrix: (A) annual prepay converting to 3-year with 20% step-down discounts; (B) mid-term 40% seat reduction in year 1; (C) full termination at month 18. Please scan and tell me which scenario is closest to what procurement expects. Happy to iterate and loop in legal for redlines.

Next steps: if you prefer option 2 or 3 we can provide precise dollar math and a DocuSign-ready amendment.

Best,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Prepay_Prorate_Matrix_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-02T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Prepay proration & rollback clauses for Engage.ai

Folks — forwarding Lisa's procurement ask and my response. Quick thoughts on negotiation posture: 
- Target option: credit roll-forward with decay (option 2) as default. It balances customer goodwill and preserves NRR profile.
- If procurement pushes hard on cash refunds, be ready to swap to a monthly pro-rata with a higher admin fee (10%) or shorten the credit window to 6 months.
- For multi-year conversion (36 months), propose a graduated early-exit slide: 75% of remaining prepay in year 1, 50% in year 2, 25% in year 3. That maps to our margin curve and is defensible.

Can Legal prepare a compact amendment: 1) credit-roll language, 2) early-exit slide table, 3) co-term true-up clause. Marcus — can you run the numbers against the current pricing in the deal record and confirm model impact? I want to keep list price uplift intact if possible.

Thanks,
Priyom

Subject: Re: Prepay proration & rollback clauses for Engage.ai

Lisa — following up with a concise set of options and the redline you can share with procurement and legal. I attached Redwood_Rollback_Clause_redline.docx with the exact language we prefer and a short commentary. TL;DR of the three options we can go to DocuSign with: 

A) Monthly pro-rata refund (low commitment): refund unused months minus 5% admin fee.
B) Credit roll-forward (recommended): credits valid for 12 months, 25% decay after year 1. No cash refunds.
C) Early-exit fee (simple, contractable): tiered percentage of remaining prepay (75/50/25 across years).

We also propose a co-term true-up clause: align renewal dates at the next invoice cycle, issue a one-time adjustment invoice for any difference, and disallow retrospective refunds when co-terming.

If procurement agrees to option B or C we'll issue an amendment and a DocuSign link for signature. If procurement needs cash refunds as a hard requirement, we can offer option A but will need to increase the admin fee to 10% or reduce the multi-year discount by 3 percentage points.

Next step: please confirm which option procurement prefers and whether legal needs any changes to the redline. If you want, I can set up a 30-minute sync with our legal lead to walk through the rollback wording.

Best,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
